content: Zinc iodide is a chemical compound consisting of the elements zinc (Zn) and iodine (I). It is classified as an inorganic compound and has a molecular weight of 319.22 g/mol. This substance appears as a white, granular, and odorless solid. It is hygroscopic, meaning it readily absorbs moisture from the surrounding atmosphere, and upon doing so, it dissolves into an aqueous solution. When exposed to high temperatures, specifically at 1150°C, zinc iodide undergoes thermal dissociation, breaking down into its constituent elements, zinc and iodine, in the vapor phase. Zinc iodide has practical applications in industrial radiography, where it is utilized as an x-ray opaque penetrant. This property enhances the contrast between damaged and intact areas in composite materials, aiding in the detection of structural defects. Additionally, zinc iodide is mentioned in United States Patent 4109065 as a component in a rechargeable aqueous zinc-halogen cell. In this application, it is part of an aqueous electrolytic solution containing a zinc salt, which may include zinc iodide, zinc bromide, or a mixture of the two. This solution is used in both the positive and negative electrode compartments of the cell.
